What Apple Headphone Notifications is — and what your listing may claim

Apple ships Headphone Notifications under Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Headphone Safety → Headphone Notifications. When enabled, the device sends an alert if cumulative headphone audio exposure exceeds the recommended 7-day loudness limit. Western indie listings often show one or more of these surfaces on the US product page. AppLocale covers paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Headphone Notifications toggle (耳机通知) — master switch that enables loud-listening exposure alerts. Gallery frames may show the Headphone Safety settings branch or a "Works with Headphone Notifications" badge.
  • Loud headphone audio exposure alerts (高音量耳机提醒) — marketing that emphasizes notifications when listening volume or duration exceeds safe thresholds over a rolling 7-day window. Screenshot overlays often show alert banners, exposure dashboards, or before/after safe-listening comparisons.
  • Hearing-health headphone volume tracking (听力健康耳机音量) — when your English listing explains that users receive warnings before cumulative exposure damages hearing. zh-Hans copy should use 听力健康 only when your US page already claims hearing-health framing — not as a generic medical guarantee.
  • Safe-listening workflows in your app — in-app audio players, podcast episodes, meditation sessions, or parental dashboards that respect or complement system Headphone Notifications when loud content plays. Screenshot overlays often show safe-listening badges on player UI or Headphone Safety settings walkthroughs.

Your gallery may lead with a Headphone Notifications toggle on one frame and an in-app exposure dashboard on the next. zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame — a Headphone Notifications alert is not a Headphone Accommodations EQ graph, not a Balance slider, and not a generic push-notification settings sheet unless that is what the screenshot shows.
